properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL — Anthony, 2026-08-31: "as reflow2 grew organically, this is mostly an effort to go back and fix STRUCTURE, not function... I had at one point discussed the possibility of each subsystem having an interface contract. but maybe before we optimize, we should restructure the code. then it would be possible to optimize performance internal to a black box." Nothing chosen.

📌 CREATED VIA create_node after searching (MOSA; black box / subsystem contract / restructure) and reading the near-matches in full — `dec:idea-what-would-a-provided-contract-buy-substitution-derived-tests-or-a-mock`, `dec:mosa-conformance`, `dec:idea-a-black-box-owes-an-interface-the-way-a-capability-owes-a-requirement`, `dec:a-black-box-needs-three-edges-not-one`. Relations drawn separately with review_relations; `add_decision`'s guard route was not usable from this client (its `related_to` argument serialises as a string here).

═══ WHY THIS IS A DIFFERENT QUESTION FROM THE 2026-08-21 ONE ═══
That node asked WHAT A CONTRACT WOULD BUY — substitution, derivable tests, a mock, optimisation — and answered that for OPTIMISATION the contract is the LEAST urgent of three needs, behind a target and a measurement. Both of those have since been supplied. This node asks the question that becomes live only now: given a target and a measurement exist, IS A CONTRACT THE THING THAT WOULD MAKE A MODULE INDEPENDENTLY OPTIMISABLE — or is it the shared struct?

═══ THE MEASUREMENT THAT PROVOKES IT (re-measured 2026-08-31) ═══
    88 core modules; 45 add methods to the SHARED `DesignGraph` struct across 62 impl blocks
    graph.rs carries 54 public methods on that one struct
    of 64 coupled pairs with no declared contract, 56 have `impl DesignGraph` on BOTH ends and ZERO cross a crate boundary

Modules own their OUTPUT TYPES and not their STATE. So a module can rework its ALGORITHMS freely and cannot rework its DATA REPRESENTATION at all. A contract at a subsystem seam does not change that, because the coupling runs through shared state rather than through the interface — which means an ICD per subsystem would document boundaries the code does not have.

═══ THE OPTIONS, none chosen ═══
① CONTRACTS FIRST, AS PROPOSED. Declare a provided contract per subsystem. Buys MOSA-style substitutability on paper and gives the seam frontier something to move. Does NOT buy independently optimisable internals while the struct is shared. Cheapest, and it is the leg reflow2 is best at.
② BREAK UP THE STRUCT. The change that would actually produce black boxes: give modules their own state behind their own accessors. Large, risky, touches everything, and nothing has yet been BLOCKED by the current shape — both budgets met so far were algorithmic, the class this structure still permits.
③ NEITHER YET — ESTABLISH THE NEED FIRST. `dec:idea-swap-dynograph-foundation-as-the-substitutability-demo` is open and is the only proposed test of whether substitution is even wanted here. Answering it would say whether ① or ② is worth anything.
④ CONTRACTS AS DOCUMENTATION, EXPLICITLY. Write them for what they genuinely buy — a published promise, a mockable double, a checkable boundary now that VERIFIES can target an Interface — and drop the claim that they enable per-module optimisation. Honest, and smaller than ① pretends to be.

⚠️ THE COUNTER-ARGUMENT TO MY OWN FRAMING, recorded beside it: `impl` blocks spread across modules is a normal and often deliberate Rust idiom for one aggregate, not automatically a defect. And nothing has yet been prevented by it — the claim that it caps optimisation is STRUCTURAL, not an observed impediment. If no optimisation is ever actually blocked, ② would be a large restructure paying for a problem nobody had.

⭐ THE TERMINOLOGY POINT FROM 2026-08-21 STILL APPLIES AND IS WORTH REPEATING: substitution is the BLACK-BOX activity (replace the inside, only the contract matters); optimisation is the WHITE-BOX activity (keep the contract, rework the inside). They are duals across one boundary, which is why one contract serves both — but they need it in opposite orders.
properties.name: OPEN — if the goal is optimisable black boxes, is the restructure that buys them breaking up the shared DesignGraph struct rather than writing a contract per subsystem?
properties.rationale: Recorded under the brainstorm discipline — ideas as ideas, nothing promoted. Raised because Anthony's proposed ordering (restructure, then optimise inside the black box) is the reverse of what the 2026-08-21 measurement concluded, and because the premise that made that conclusion actionable has since changed: the target and the measurement he lacked then now exist, so the question genuinely reopens rather than merely repeating.
